parole.testo: Derived from Proto-Mongolic *adalï (“similar, same as”). Compare Mongolian адил (adil, “similar”), Mogholi آدَال (ādāl /⁠adali⁠/, “similar”), and Mongghul dali.

Ultimately from Proto-Mongolic *bödene, via a Turkic source. Compare Kazakh бөдене (bödene), Tatar бүдәнә (büdänä), Uyghur بودۇنە (bodune), Uzbek bedana, boʻdana, Turkmen bedene. Borrowed from a Southern Mongolic dialect of Middle Mongol ancestral to Mongghul funige (“fox”), from Proto-Mongolic *hünegen (“fox”).

Ultimately from Proto-Mongolic *girgaxul, via a Turkic source. Compare Azerbaijani qırqovul, Chagatai قرغاول (qirǧawul), Uyghur قىرغۇل (qirghul), Uzbek qirgʻovul, Kazakh қырғауыл (qırğawıl), Kyrgyz кыргоол (kırgool), Tatar кыргавыл (qırğawıl), Bashkir ҡырғауыл (qırğawıl).
Ultimately derived from Proto-Mongolic *kaïčï, compare Mongolian хайч (xajč). Likely via Chagatai or Old Anatolian Turkish.
